title: Alert first responder cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference for the on-call / first-responder when a performance alert (latency/throughput/error rate) fires for the serving runtime. Focus: get to safe state, collect evidence for next-level debug, decide whether to roll back or mitigate.

Audience:
on-call engineers, SREs, on-call serving-runtime owners, any engineer asked to do the initial triage.

Scope / Assumptions:
- Applicable to hosted + dedicated clusters.
- Alert types covered: p50/p95/p99 token latency spikes, QPS drop, increased error rate (5xx), throughput degradation, GPU saturation alerts.
- We assume Grafana + Prometheus metrics, Jaeger traces (or X-Ray), and request-level traces logged to our tracing store.

FIRST 10 MINUTES (the checklist you can do while on Slack):
1) Acknowledge alert + gather context:
   - Note: which alert fired (name + rule) and timestamp window.
   - Open Grafana dashboard: "Serving / Latency & Throughput" and the alert panel.
   - Check whether multiple regions/models are affected or single model/route.

2) Quick triage questions (answer these fast):
   - Is this new code/deploy/canary rolled out recently? (check CI/CD, last deploy id)
   - Is there a correlated infra event? (k8s node termination, noisy neighbor, AZ outage)
   - Is the traffic shape abnormal? (sudden spike in seq length, batch size, or tokens)

3) Snapshot essential signals (copy these into the incident thread):
   - Top impacted model(s) and model-version IDs.
   - Percent increase in p95/p99 vs baseline (last 6h).
   - GPU util / memory pressure on affected pods.
   - Error-rate and error types (trace IDs for first errors).
   - Recent config changes: batching config, quantization toggles, kernel flags.

QUICK COMMANDS / QUERIES (paste into terminal / grafana PromQL):
- p95 latency over last 30m for model X (PromQL):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{model="MODEL_X"}[5m])) by (le))
- QPS for route Y: 
  sum(rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (model)
- GPU util (node level): 
  avg(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent{job="node-exporter"}) by (instance)
- Tail errors (last 1h) from logging index (elastic):
  query: log_level:ERROR AND model_id:MODEL_X sort:@timestamp desc limit 50

IF IT LOOKS INFRA:
- Check node autoscaler events and k8s pod restarts: kubectl get events --namespace=redwood-serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
- Verify network errors: cloud provider metrics for packet drops, retries, LB 5xx rates.
- If GPU OOMs appear, note pod id and host and collect /var/log/nvidia* and dmesg.

IF IT LOOKS CODE / MODEL:
- Check recent commits and PRs on the path (last successful deploy id).
- Identify whether a model variant was swapped (quantized vs base).
- Validate config differences between canary and main (batching thresholds, token limit, compile flags).

BISect (narrow a causal change) — quick plan for first responder:
1) Reproduce: attempt to replay a small sample of requests that triggered the spike using the perf harness (perf-invoker). Use the same prompt distribution (copy earliest 10 failing trace IDs).
   - Command (local perf harness): ./perf-invoker --model MODEL_X --concurrency 4 --seq-dist sample_prompts.json --warmup 50 --duration 120
2) If reproduced on canary only: do a traffic split rollback (route 100% to baseline variant) OR pause canary. If on baseline: check for infra regressions or config rollouts.
3) Bisect deployment window: binary search through deploys between last-known-good and first-bad. If deploy ids are A...F, trigger a canary with earlier commit and run the perf-invoker for short run.
   - Use the playbook: test commit mid-point for 10–20 runs; if still bad, walk midpoint lower; else move up.
   - Record results in the incident thread with commit SHAs and summary metrics (p95, p99, median, GPU util).

CANARY-COMPARISON CHECKLIST (what to compare side-by-side):
- Token length distribution (median and tail) — a heavier tail can blow up p99.
- Batching behavior: effective batch sizes seen in the canary vs baseline.
- KV cache hit rates (if caching enabled).
- Memory usage, per-process swap, and mmap counts.
- CUDA kernel fallbacks or mixed-precision differences in logs.
- Quantization backend used (int8 / fp16 / bf16) and whether auto-fallback occurred.
- Sequence-level trace time split: tokenization / attention / kernel time / io time.

TRACING / PROFILE COLLECTION (grab these quickly):
- Increase tracing sampling for affected routes (temporarily) to 5–10% to capture representative traces.
- Export top slow trace IDs to the incident channel.
- Run a heap/snapshot on one affected process if memory suspected.
- Capture nvprof / Nsight logs only on a repro node — coordinate with infra if it's high-cost.

ESCALATION TRIGGERS (when to page the oncall-SRE or runtime-engineering):
- Can't reproduce with perf-invoker but production shows persistent p99 > baseline by >2x for 30+ minutes.
- Evidence of model runtime fallback (kernel or precision fallback) or CUDA errors in pod logs.
- Multiple models/regions impacted simultaneously (likely infra).
- Rollback failed or can't be performed safely.

MITIGATION OPTIONS (fast, medium, slow):
- Fast: pause canary, route traffic away from affected model-version, increase replicas to lower queueing (short-term only).
- Medium: rollback to last-good deploy, toggle batching threshold lower to reduce max latency.
- Slow: schedule deeper bench + profiling, follow full bisect plan, onboard model rollback in Dedicated reserved pools.

POST-MORTEM DATA TO COLLECT (for follow-up):
- Golden prompt set run results (baseline vs offending) with token-level breakdown.
- Full trace dumps for top 50 slow traces.
- Perf harness logs and exact command-line used for reproduction.
- Deploy IDs and diff summary (config + code + model binary).
- Grafana snapshots (6h baseline vs incident period) for p50/p95/p99, QPS, GPU util.

NOTES TO SELF / TYPICAL GOTCHAS:
- A small increase in average token length often multiplies p99 latency under batching — check batching effective windows.
- Quantized kernels can degrade latency on the tail if they trigger a fallback path for specific ops.
- Autoscaler oscillation can cause transient p95 spikes; correlate pod churn with latency spikes.
- Network retries increase perceived latency even when GPUs are idle.

EXAMPLE INCIDENT MINUTE-LOG (copy into pager duty thread):
- 09:12: alert p99-latency-model-X fired (p99=2.8s, baseline=0.9s)
- 09:13: opened dashboard, CPU/GPU util normal, but batch size single-threaded mode increased
- 09:17: collected 20 slow trace IDs, perf-invoker reproduced 2.5x p95 locally on canary commit C123
- 09:35: paused canary (traffic -> baseline), p99 trending back to baseline by 09:50
- Action: rollback canary and open follow-up ticket INF-1423 for root-cause analysis

FOLLOW-UP TICKETING / HOW TO WRITE THE RCA NOTES:
- Summarize timeline + key metrics first (p50/p95/p99, QPS, GPU util).
- Attach diffs for deploys, link to reproducer run, attach traces and logs.
- Include hypothesis tested and how bisect resolved or narrowed to specific change.

TODO / items to add to runbook later:
- Quick shell script to collect all required logs and traces given a pod id.
- Standardized perf-invoker prompt sets per product vertical.
- Dashboard panel templates with prebuilt comparison snapshot links (canary vs baseline).

END

(If you follow this checklist you should be able to get to a safe state and hand off to the runtime team with reproducible evidence.)
